Rhythmicity analysis using Harmonic Regression and bootstrapping

Source: R/rhythmicity.R
rhythmicity.Rd

rhythmicity applies harmonic regression to the variables and calculates confidence intervals using bootstrapping. The intervals are corrected using bonferroni method in the end.

Usage

rhythmicity(
  input,
  operation,
  seed = NA,
  tau = 24,
  num_boot,
  alpha = 0.05,
  fc_cutoff
)

Arguments

input

Matrix, where columns correspond to variables and rows correspond to samples w.r.t time.

operation

Anyone of the following should be provided: "matrix" or "column". Do not use "matrix" mode when there are missing values in the matrix, instead use "column" mode.

seed

Is used to reproduce the same results across multiple runs.

tau

The period of oscillation.

num_boot

The number of bootstrap samples to be generated.

alpha

The significance level to estimate the confidence level. Default is 0.05.

fc_cutoff

The amplitude cutoff to define the rhythmic status of variables (genes and other).

Value

A list for each subject containing the following: a lower (ci.lower) and upper (ci.upper) value of the confidence interval of the amplitude, the rhythmic status of each variable (rhythmicity), mesor from harmonic regression (hr.mesor), amplitude from harmonic regression (hr.amplitude), and phase from harmonic regression (hr.phase).

Details

A matrix with samples across time in rows and with columns of variables are to be provided to perform harmonic regression. After regressing the data with cosine functions, the best fit and the residuals are obtained. The residuals are then sampled with replacement using bootstrapping. In each instance of bootstrapping, the sampled residuals are summed to the best fit yielding a bootstrap estimate of amplitude. The Confidence Interval (CI) for amplitude estimates will be computed using the provided alpha value (also includes Bonferroni correction). Using the CI and fc_cutoff the rhythmic status of each variables are defined as follows: rhythmic (if the lower and upper CI lies above the cutoff), arrhythmic (if the lower and upper CI lies below or is equal to the cutoff) and inconclusive (if the lower and upper CI straddles the cutoff). The obtained mesor (the average value), amplitude, and phase is estimated before bootstrapping.

Please note that at least 4 samples are needed per subject. Only the variables with at least 4 samples will be analyzed. The column-wise operation will need more time than matrix-wise operation.

Author

Jayanth Sreekanth

Examples


# Load the data that comes along with the package and run rhythmicity.
# This data was generated using simphony.

data(simdf)

suppressWarnings(

output_hr <- rhythmicity(input = simdf,
                         operation = "matrix",
                         seed = 7,
                         tau = 24, #value in general for humans
                         num_boot = 999,
                         alpha = 0.05,
                         fc_cutoff = 0.5)

)
